cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Permanent joints cannot be disassembled without damage: welding, brazing, soft soldering, riveting and adhesive bonding.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Temporary joints can be repeatedly assembled and disassembled: bolts, nuts, screws, clips and captive fasteners.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Welding fuses metals together by melting the parent material (and usually a filler rod); MIG, TIG and MMA are common arc welding processes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Brazing joins metals by melting a filler (brass alloy, above 450 degrees C) that flows by capillary action between closely fitting parts.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Soft soldering joins metals with a tin-lead or lead-free alloy (below 450 degrees C); used for electronics and light sheet metal.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Threaded fasteners (bolts, nuts, studs, machine screws) provide strong, adjustable and removable joints.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Rivets are permanent mechanical fasteners: solid, blind (pop) and semi-tubular types are common in engineering.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: MIG welding (Metal Inert Gas) feeds a continuous wire electrode with shielding gas; fast and versatile for steel and aluminium.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: TIG welding (Tungsten Inert Gas) uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode; produces high-quality, precise welds suitable for thin materials.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Adhesive bonding (epoxy, cyanoacrylate, anaerobic) can join dissimilar materials and distribute stress evenly.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Joint design depends on: required strength, whether disassembly is needed, materials being joined, operating conditions and cost.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Joining & Assembly
cards.back: Heat-affected zone (HAZ) near a weld has altered properties due to the thermal cycle; it can be weaker or more brittle than the parent metal.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — joining & assembly?
cards.back: 1. For Joining & Assembly questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Joining & Assembly through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
